newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hashimoto invites Chinese president to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto invites Chinese president to Japan.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Sunday invited Chinese President Jiang Zemin to pay a state visit to Japan next year, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said.

"Prime Minister Hashimoto expressed the hope that President Jiang Zemin can visit Japan next year, the 25th anniversary of the resumption of diplomatic relations between the two countries," Shen told a news briefing.
"President Jiang Zemin expressed the hope that Prime Minister Hashimoto can also visit China at a convenient time," he said.
The two leaders are in the Philippines for the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Sino-Japanese relations have been strained in recent months by a row over disputed islands in the East China Sea, known as the Diaoyus by China and Taiwan and the Senkakus by Japan, and by a visit Hashimoto paid to a controversial shrine honouring Japan's war dead.
Hashimoto said earlier this month that his new government, formed after general elections in October, would regard improving relations between Tokyo and Beijing as a priority.
